units: all true_* dimensions are in micrometres of real tissue

oxyntic_gland.source: normal gastric body mucosal thickness; foveolar compartment 0.2 mm and glandular compartment 0.6 mm, foveola:gland ratio 1:4 (normal values tabulated in Gastroenterology 1993;104:1310)

pyloric_gland.source: normal gastric antral mucosal thickness, foveolar compartment 0.4 mm, i.e. a roughly 1:1 pit:gland ratio (same source)

gland_density_note: a RESULT of the assumed spacing, not a measured density; no measured human gastric gland density was located in this build

mucus_barrier.which_measurement: HUMAN antrum, in vivo, mean 106 um (minimum 50)
mucus_barrier.source: adherent gastrointestinal mucus gel thickness measured in vivo; HUMAN antrum mean 106 um.  Atuma et al., Am J Physiol Gastrointest Liver Physiol 2001;280:G922, doi:10.1152/ajpgi.2001.280.5.G922
mucus_barrier.why_not_200um: the micro view is built at the HUMAN antral thickness (106 um) because it is the only human in-vivo measurement in that study.  The frequently quoted ~200 um is the rat corpus value and is shown alongside it, labelled as rat, rather than being used as if human.
mucus_barrier.pH_profile_shape: LINEAR IN pH across the gel
mucus_barrier.pH_profile_caveat: the real juxtamucosal profile is sigmoid, set by the balance of H+ back-diffusion against HCO3- secretion.  No reaction-diffusion equation is solved here; the two published endpoints are interpolated linearly in pH and that is declared on the page itself.

proton_gradient_factor.note: computed from the declared endpoints, not restated from a textbook: a luminal pH of 1.5 against a surface pH of 7.0 is a 3.16e+05-fold hydrogen-ion concentration difference across the barrier, and a luminal pH of 3.5 is 3.16e+03-fold.  The commonly quoted "10^4" sits inside this span but is not the only answer; the factor depends entirely on which luminal pH is assumed.

cell_axis: the pit lining and the gastric surface; secretes the mucus-bicarbonate gel
neck and upper gland body; H+/K+-ATPase on the APICAL membrane plus intrinsic factor

regional_gland_type.antrum: pyloric glands: mucous + G cells + D cells, essentially no parietal cells

proton_pump.membrane: APICAL (luminal) membrane of the parietal cell, and the tubulovesicles that fuse with it on stimulation
proton_pump.why_it_matters: it is the final common step of acid secretion, downstream of the histamine H2, gastrin/CCK2 and muscarinic M3 receptors, which is why irreversible inhibition of the pump by a proton pump inhibitor raises intragastric pH far more completely than H2 receptor blockade
proton_pump.ppi_mechanism: PPIs are acid-labile prodrugs: they are absorbed in the small intestine, reach the parietal cell through the blood, and are protonated and trapped in the acidic secretory canaliculus, where they rearrange to a thiophilic sulfenamide and bind covalently to cysteines on the pump alpha subunit.  Acid secretion then recovers only as new pump protein is made.
proton_pump.expression_source: ATP4A/ATP4B are read from CELLxGENE Census as ADDITIONAL genes, reported separately from the 61-gene ADME panel

secretagogue_cells.ECL_cell: histamine, acting on parietal-cell H2 receptors
secretagogue_cells.G_cell: gastrin, from the ANTRUM, acting on CCK2 receptors
secretagogue_cells.D_cell: somatostatin, the brake on both G and parietal cells

scale_check.statement: the gland column is drawn at 60x and the mucus gel at 480x in the nested inset.  Both factors are shown in the HUD; nothing in the micro view is at organ scale and the page never implies it is.
